steps: Stamen is the male reproductive part of a flower; carpel is the female reproductive part.
A stamen consists of an anther and a filament; a carpel consists of a stigma, style and ovary.
The anther produces pollen grains; the ovary contains ovules.
Pollen grains contain the male gametes; the ovule contains the female gamete (egg).
items.finalAnswer: The stamen is the male reproductive part of a flower, while the carpel is the female reproductive part.

steps: In binary fission, the DNA of a bacterial cell replicates.
The cell elongates, and the two DNA copies move apart.
The cell membrane and cell wall grow inward between the two DNA copies, forming a partition.
The parent cell divides into two daughter cells, each with a copy of the DNA.
The daughter bacteria are genetically identical to the parent cell, except for any mutations.
items.finalAnswer: In binary fission, a bacterium copies its DNA and divides into two daughter bacteria, each receiving one copy.

steps: Vegetative propagation is a type of asexual reproduction in which new plants develop from the vegetative parts of a parent plant, such as roots, stems or leaves.
Modified stems: underground stems store food and bear buds that can grow into new plants; examples include potato tubers, ginger rhizomes and onion bulbs.
Modified roots: roots of some plants store food and can grow into new plants; an example is sweet potato.
Modified leaves: buds on the leaf margins grow into plantlets that can develop into new plants; an example is Bryophyllum.
items.finalAnswer: Vegetative propagation produces new plants from vegetative parts of a parent plant, including modified stems, roots and leaves.

steps: Humans can produce new plants artificially by vegetative propagation using parts of parent plants.
In cutting, a piece of stem, root or leaf is planted; it develops roots and shoots and grows into a new plant.
In layering, a branch is bent and covered with soil while it is still attached to the parent plant; after roots develop, it is cut off and planted separately.
In grafting, a shoot or twig (scion) of one plant is joined to the rooted stem (stock) of another plant so that they grow together.
In tissue culture, a small piece of plant tissue is grown on a sterile nutrient medium to produce many new plants.
items.finalAnswer: New plants can be grown from vegetative parts by cutting, layering, grafting and tissue culture.

steps: The sporophyte is the diploid generation of a plant that produces spores by meiosis.
The gametophyte is the haploid generation of a plant that develops from a spore and produces gametes by mitosis.
The sporophyte produces spores, which grow into gametophytes.
The gametophyte produces male and female gametes; their fusion forms a diploid zygote that develops into a sporophyte.
items.finalAnswer: The sporophyte produces spores, and the gametophyte produces gametes; together they form the two alternating generations in a plant’s life cycle.

steps: Flowering plants show alternation of generations between a diploid sporophyte and haploid gametophytes.
The mature flowering plant is the sporophyte. In its flowers, meiosis produces haploid spores.
Microspores develop into pollen grains, the male gametophytes; a megaspore develops into the embryo sac, the female gametophyte.
The pollen grain delivers male gametes to the embryo sac. Fertilization forms a diploid zygote.
The zygote develops into an embryo in the seed. When the seed germinates, the embryo grows into a new sporophyte.
items.finalAnswer: Flowering plants alternate between a diploid sporophyte that produces spores and haploid gametophytes that produce gametes.

steps: Inside the ovule, a diploid megaspore mother cell undergoes meiosis to form four haploid megaspores.
Three megaspores degenerate, leaving one functional megaspore.
The functional megaspore undergoes three mitotic divisions, producing eight haploid nuclei.
The nuclei become arranged in a seven-celled embryo sac: an egg cell and two synergids at one end, three antipodal cells at the other end, and a central cell containing two polar nuclei.
The embryo sac is the female gametophyte of the flowering plant.
items.finalAnswer: The embryo sac develops from one functional megaspore through three mitotic divisions and consists of seven cells with eight nuclei.
